policies.title: Expenses
rules: The daily meal allowance while travelling is USD 70 for domestic trips and USD 95 for international trips.
When a client provides a meal, the daily meal allowance is reduced by USD 20 for each meal provided; reductions for several meals on the same day combine.
Any expense above USD 25 needs an itemised receipt submitted within 30 days of the purchase.
Any single expense above USD 500 needs written approval from the employee's manager before it is incurred.
Client entertainment is capped at USD 120 per person per event and needs director approval; a meal charged as client entertainment cannot also be claimed under the daily meal allowance.
Alcohol is never reimbursable.
Certification exam fees are reimbursed in full on a passing result and for one retake per exam; this reimbursement is separate from, and combines with, the certification bonus.

policies.title: Travel
rules: Flights shorter than 6 hours are booked in economy; flights of 6 hours or more may be booked in premium economy.
Hotel nights are capped at USD 210, or USD 290 in New York, San Francisco, London and Sydney.
Flights and hotels should be booked 14 days or more before departure where the client schedule allows.
A rental car is allowed when no public transit connects the airport to the client site; use of a personal vehicle is reimbursed at USD 0.67 per mile.
Mileage reimbursement cannot be combined with rental car or fuel claims on the same trip.
Non-billable travel of more than 3 hours on a weekend earns a half day of time off in lieu, to be taken within 60 days.
Travel billed to a client follows the client's travel policy where that policy is stricter than this one; the stricter rule applies and the two do not combine.

policies.title: Remote Work
rules: Employees may work from home up to 3 days per week; during client-site weeks the client's schedule takes precedence.
Fully remote arrangements need director approval and are reviewed every 6 months.
Core hours are 10:00 to 15:00 in the employee's local time zone.
A home-office stipend of USD 600 is paid once, when the employee joins.
An internet allowance of USD 45 per month is paid to employees working remotely; it combines with the home-office stipend because they are separate budgets.
Coworking memberships are reimbursed up to USD 180 per month, but in any month where coworking is claimed the internet allowance is not paid, so the two do not combine.
Working from abroad is permitted for up to 20 days per calendar year in a country without a company office, with HR and security approval requested 10 business days or more in advance.
Client data must never be accessed over public wi-fi, wherever the employee is working.

policies.title: Certification Bonus
rules: Associate tier: USD 200 for each Salesforce Certified Associate or Salesforce Certified AI Associate credential.
Administrator tier: USD 350 for each Administrator-level credential, including Salesforce Certified Administrator, Advanced Administrator and Marketing Cloud Administrator.

Specialist tier: USD 400 for each Salesforce credential named Specialist, such as Agentforce Specialist and Marketing Cloud Email Specialist; Tableau Desktop Specialist belongs to the Tableau tier instead.

Consultant tier: USD 500 for each Salesforce Certified Consultant credential, such as the Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, Revenue Cloud and Marketing Cloud Consultant credentials.
Developer tier: USD 600 for each Salesforce Certified Platform Developer credential (I or II); MuleSoft Certified Developer belongs to the MuleSoft tier instead.

Architect tier: USD 900 for each Salesforce Certified Architect credential, such as Application, Data, Integration, and Identity and Access Management Architect; Salesforce Certified Technical Architect is paid USD 2,400 and is not also paid at the Architect tier, and MuleSoft architect credentials belong to the MuleSoft tier.

Tableau and MuleSoft tiers: USD 450 for each Tableau credential of any level, including Tableau Certified Data Analyst and Tableau Desktop Specialist, and USD 550 for each MuleSoft credential, including MuleSoft Certified Developer, MuleSoft Certified Platform Architect and MuleSoft Certified Integration Architect.
Each certification is paid once, in the payroll run after the certificate date; bonuses for several held certifications stack, and no bonus is paid again for a renewal or retake.

policies.title: On-Call
rules: On-call rotations run for one week, from Monday 09:00 to the following Monday 09:00 in the on-call engineer's local time.
A weekly on-call allowance of USD 320 is paid for each rotation week served.
Priority 1 incidents must be acknowledged within 30 minutes and Priority 2 incidents within 2 hours.
A call-out payment of USD 60 is paid for each Priority 1 incident handled between 18:00 and 08:00 or on a weekend; it combines with the weekly allowance.

During a client go-live week, a go-live support premium of USD 150 per day replaces the call-out payment for that day; the premium combines with the weekly allowance but not with the call-out payment.
An employee who handles an incident between 22:00 and 06:00 may start work 11 hours after the incident closes without any loss of pay.
No employee is placed on call in two consecutive weeks, and rotation swaps need manager approval 48 hours before the rotation starts.

policies.title: Data Security
rules: Client data must stay inside the client's Salesforce org, an approved sandbox or the firm's encrypted project drive, and must never be stored on personal devices.
All laptops use full-disk encryption, and multi-factor authentication is mandatory on every work account.
Production data copied into a sandbox must be masked before any developer or tester can access the sandbox.
Use of the firm-approved password manager is mandatory; passwords are never shared in chat or email.
A lost or stolen device must be reported to the security lead within 2 hours.
Access to a client org is removed within 1 business day of the project end date or of an employee's departure.
Security awareness training must be completed within 30 days of joining and every 12 months afterwards.

A suspected data breach is reported to the security lead within 4 hours and the client is notified within 48 hours of confirmation; if the client contract sets a shorter notice period, the shorter period applies instead.

runbooks.purpose: Refreshes a Full sandbox from production and ensures client data is masked before any developer or tester can see it. It keeps the sandbox usable for the next release cycle and meets the firm's data security rule on masking.
prerequisites: At least 29 days have passed since the previous Full sandbox refresh
A SandboxPostCopy Apex class that masks personal data has been tested in a Partial sandbox
A change freeze has been agreed with the client business owner
A list of named credentials and external endpoints that must be re-pointed after the refresh
System Administrator access to production and to the sandbox

steps.action: Announce a change freeze to all developers and testers at least 2 business days before the refresh date.
steps.verification: Every developer has acknowledged the freeze message in the project channel.

steps.action: Export sandbox-only configuration that is not in source control, such as custom setting values and email templates.
steps.verification: The exported file row counts match the counts shown in the sandbox before the refresh.

steps.action: In Setup, open Sandboxes, choose Refresh on the Full sandbox and select the SandboxPostCopy class in the Apex class field.
steps.verification: The sandbox status changes to Pending and then Processing.

steps.action: Wait for the sandbox refresh completion email sent to the System Administrator.
steps.verification: The sandbox status shows Completed and the completion email has arrived.

steps.action: Log in to the refreshed sandbox and query Contact email addresses and phone numbers.
steps.verification: No email address is outside the example.invalid domain and no phone number matches a production value.

steps.action: Re-point named credentials and external endpoints to the client's test systems.
steps.verification: A test callout from Developer Console returns HTTP 200 from each test endpoint.

steps.action: Reload the exported sandbox-only configuration.
steps.verification: Row counts after the load match the counts from the export file.

steps.action: Set Email Deliverability to System email only and lift the change freeze.
steps.verification: Setup shows the Access level as System email only and the lift message is posted to the project channel.

rollback_steps: If masking has not run, immediately set Email Deliverability to No access and revoke sandbox logins for all users except the System Administrator.
Delete the refreshed sandbox and re-create it from the sandbox clone taken before the refresh, if one exists.
Re-run the SandboxPostCopy class manually from Developer Console and repeat the masking verification query.
Keep the change freeze in place and notify the client business owner of the new availability date.

known_issues.symptom: Refresh button is greyed out with the message 'You can refresh this sandbox in 14 days'
known_issues.resolution: The Full sandbox refresh interval has not passed; wait for the date shown or use a Partial sandbox for the work.

known_issues.symptom: SandboxPostCopy fails with 'System.LimitException: Too many DML rows: 10001'
known_issues.resolution: Rewrite the masking class to run as a Batchable with a scope of 200 and re-run it from Developer Console.

known_issues.symptom: Named credential callout returns 'CalloutException: Unauthorized endpoint'
known_issues.resolution: Add the test endpoint URL to Remote Site Settings or to the named credential and retry the callout.

runbooks.title: Change Set Deployment to Production
runbooks.purpose: Moves a defined group of metadata components from a sandbox to production using an outbound change set. It is used by smaller releases where the client does not run source control.
prerequisites: A deployment connection is authorised between the sandbox and production
The change set contents have been approved by the client business owner
All Apex tests in the sandbox pass with at least 85 percent coverage on the changed classes
A deployment window of at least 90 minutes is booked outside client peak hours

steps.action: Create an outbound change set named with the release number and add each approved component.
steps.verification: The component list matches the release checklist item for item.

steps.action: Use View/Add Dependencies to add any missing dependent components.
steps.verification: The dependency list shows no unresolved components.

steps.action: Upload the change set to the production org.
steps.verification: The status shows Uploaded and an inbound change set appears in production.

steps.action: In production, run Validate on the inbound change set with the RunLocalTests option.
steps.verification: The validation result shows Succeeded with all tests passing.

steps.action: Capture the validation ID and screenshot the test results for the release file.
steps.verification: The release file contains the validation ID and the screenshot.

steps.action: Deploy the validated inbound change set inside the agreed window.
steps.verification: The Deployment Status page shows Succeeded with 0 component failures.

steps.action: Run the smoke test script covering the changed page layouts, fields and automation.
steps.verification: All smoke test cases are marked passed by the tester.

steps.action: Post the deployment outcome to the project channel and start the 24 hour monitoring window.
steps.verification: The Setup Audit Trail shows only the expected changes and the channel post is visible.

steps.action: Check Apex Exception Emails and Debug Logs at the end of the 24 hour monitoring window.
steps.verification: No new unhandled exceptions are listed for the deployed components.

rollback_steps: Stop any further changes to production and notify the client business owner.
Reverse the change by building an outbound change set from the sandbox state before the release.
Deactivate any deployed Flow or Apex trigger manually in production if it causes errors.
Redeploy the earlier change set, validate it and deploy it in a new window.
Record the failure cause in the release file for the post-release review.

known_issues.symptom: Deployment fails with 'Average test coverage across all Apex Classes and Triggers is 74%, at least 75% Apex code coverage is required'
known_issues.resolution: Add test classes for the uncovered classes in the sandbox, upload a new change set and validate again.

known_issues.symptom: Error 'Cannot delete component: in use by another component'
known_issues.resolution: Change sets cannot delete components, so remove the reference first and delete the component manually in production after the deployment.

known_issues.symptom: Upload is not visible in production and the inbound list is empty
known_issues.resolution: Wait up to 30 minutes for the upload to be processed and confirm the deployment connection is authorised in both orgs.

runbooks.title: Salesforce CLI Metadata Deployment from Source Control
runbooks.purpose: Deploys tagged source from the Git repository to a target org using the Salesforce CLI with a validated quick deploy. It gives a repeatable and auditable path for client projects that use source control.
prerequisites: Salesforce CLI is installed and updated to the version listed in the project repository
The release branch is merged and tagged with the release number
The target org is authorised with an alias using the JWT flow or web login
A package manifest file lists every component in the release
Apex tests for the changed classes pass in a scratch org or sandbox

steps.action: Check out the release tag and confirm the working tree is clean.
steps.verification: git status reports nothing to commit and the tag name matches the release number.

steps.action: Run sf org list and confirm the target alias is connected.
steps.verification: The target alias shows Connected with the expected username.

steps.action: Retrieve the current production metadata for the manifest into a temporary folder.
steps.verification: The retrieve command returns Succeeded and the folder contains the manifest components.

steps.action: Compare the retrieved metadata with the release source to identify unintended changes.
steps.verification: The diff shows only the components in the release checklist.

steps.action: Run sf project deploy start with the --dry-run flag, the manifest and the RunLocalTests test level.
steps.verification: The output shows Status Succeeded with all tests passing.

steps.action: Note the validated job ID from the dry run output.
steps.verification: The job ID is recorded in the release file.

steps.action: Run sf project deploy quick with the validated job ID inside the deployment window.
steps.verification: The command returns Succeeded and the Deployment Status page agrees.

steps.action: Run the automated smoke test suite against the target org.
steps.verification: The suite finishes with 0 failures.

steps.action: Start a 4 hour monitoring window and watch Apex Exception Emails and the Event Log.
steps.verification: No new exception emails are received for the deployed components.

steps.action: Tag the deployment in the Git repository with the date and the target alias.
steps.verification: The tag is visible in the remote repository.

steps.action: Close the 4 hour monitoring window and post the summary to the project channel.
steps.verification: The summary post lists the job ID and the test results.

rollback_steps: Stop further deployments and notify the delivery manager.
Check out the previous release tag in the repository.
Run a validate-only deployment of the previous tag with RunLocalTests.
Quick deploy the validated previous release job to restore the earlier metadata.
Manually remove any new components that the previous tag does not contain using a destructive changes manifest.

known_issues.symptom: Quick deploy fails with 'The validation ID is not valid or has expired'
known_issues.resolution: A validation is usable for 10 days only after it succeeds; run the dry run again and quick deploy the new job ID.

known_issues.symptom: Deploy fails with 'INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY: invalid cross reference id'
known_issues.resolution: A referenced profile, queue or user does not exist in the target org; add the missing component to the manifest or create it first.

known_issues.symptom: Command returns 'ERROR running project deploy start: expired access/refresh token'
known_issues.resolution: Log in to the org again with sf org login jwt or web and rerun the command.

known_issues.symptom: Test failure 'System.LimitException: Too many SOQL queries: 101'
known_issues.resolution: Bulkify the failing Apex code, move queries outside loops and run the tests again.

runbooks.title: Permission Set and Permission Set Group Change
runbooks.purpose: Applies approved changes to permission sets and permission set groups so users gain or lose access in a controlled way. It reduces the risk of over-permissioning and of broken access to key objects after a release.
prerequisites: A signed access change request listing users, permission sets and the reason for the change
The permission set changes have been tested in a sandbox with a representative user
The access matrix document is up to date
System Administrator access to production

steps.action: Compare the requested access with the current access matrix.
steps.verification: Each requested change is mapped to a named permission set in the matrix.

steps.action: Make the changes in the sandbox permission set and permission set group and recalculate the group.
steps.verification: The group status shows Updated, not Updating or Failed.

steps.action: Log in as a test user in the sandbox and test each object and field affected.
steps.verification: The test log shows access granted or removed as requested.

steps.action: Deploy the permission set metadata to production through the agreed deployment method.
steps.verification: The Deployment Status shows Succeeded.

steps.action: Assign or remove the permission set group for the listed users using a bulk assignment.
steps.verification: The Assigned Users list matches the access change request.

steps.action: Run a SOQL query on PermissionSetAssignment for the affected users.
steps.verification: The query results agree with the request line by line.

steps.action: Start a 48 hour monitoring window and review the Login History and support requests for access errors.
steps.verification: No insufficient access errors are raised by affected users in the 48 hour window.

rollback_steps: Remove the new permission set group assignments for the affected users.
Reassign the previous permission set group to the affected users.
Deploy the previous permission set metadata version from source control.
Ask two affected users to confirm that their earlier access is restored.

known_issues.symptom: Assignment fails with 'INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS_OR_READONLY' for a user
known_issues.resolution: The user licence does not allow the permissions in the set; assign a compatible licence or remove the incompatible permission.

known_issues.symptom: Group status stays at Updating for more than 30 minutes
known_issues.resolution: Open the group, choose Recalculate and wait for Updated; if it fails, edit the group again and save.

known_issues.symptom: Deployment error 'You cannot assign a permission set that has the Modify All Data permission to this user profile'
known_issues.resolution: Remove the broad permission from the set or move the user to a profile that supports it after client approval.

runbooks.title: Agentforce Agent Rollout to Production
runbooks.purpose: Moves a tested Agentforce agent from a sandbox into production and activates it for a defined user group. It ensures topics, actions and guardrails behave as designed before real customers or staff reach the agent.
prerequisites: The agent passed at least 100 of the 120 scripted test conversations in the sandbox
Agentforce capacity is purchased and enabled in production
The client has approved the knowledge articles the agent relies on
Every Apex action and Flow used by the agent has been deployed to production
An escalation queue exists and is staffed during the launch week

steps.action: Freeze changes to agent topics, instructions and actions in the sandbox.
steps.verification: The agent version in the sandbox is labelled with the release number.

steps.action: Deploy the agent metadata, topics and actions to production using the Salesforce CLI Metadata Deployment from Source Control runbook.
steps.verification: The deployment shows Succeeded with 0 component failures.

steps.action: Confirm that the data library or knowledge source used for grounding is indexed in production.
steps.verification: A test search in the Agentforce Builder returns the expected articles.

steps.action: Assign the Agentforce permission sets to the pilot user group.
steps.verification: The pilot users appear under Assigned Users for the permission set.

steps.action: Run 20 smoke test conversations in the Agentforce Builder against the production configuration.
steps.verification: All 20 conversations choose the expected topic and action.

steps.action: Test each guardrail and the escalation rule with an out-of-scope request.
steps.verification: The agent declines the request and hands off to the escalation queue.

steps.action: Activate the agent version for the pilot user group.
steps.verification: The agent status shows Active in Setup.

steps.action: Enable the agent in the client channel such as the Experience Cloud site or the messaging deployment.
steps.verification: A test chat from the channel reaches the agent.

steps.action: Open the Einstein Trust Layer audit trail and confirm masking and logging are on.
steps.verification: A sample conversation appears in the audit data with masked personal values.

steps.action: Begin the 72 hour monitoring window and review the conversation logs every 8 hours on the first day.
steps.verification: The review log has an entry for each check.

steps.action: Review the escalation rate and the topic misses against the thresholds in the use-case brief.
steps.verification: Both measures are within the agreed thresholds or a tuning item is raised.

steps.action: At the end of the 72 hour window, hold a go or no-go review with the client business owner.

rollback_steps: Deactivate the agent version in Setup.
Disable the agent in the client channel so that users see the standard contact route.
Remove the Agentforce permission sets from the pilot group.
Reactivate the previous agent version if one exists and rerun the 20 smoke tests.
Send a summary of failed conversations to the agent designer for tuning.

known_issues.symptom: Activation fails with 'Agent cannot be activated: one or more actions are missing or inactive'
known_issues.resolution: Deploy and activate the missing Flow or Apex action in production, then activate the agent again.

known_issues.symptom: Agent replies 'I'm sorry, I can't help with that' to an in-scope question
known_issues.resolution: Review the topic classification description and add scope phrases, then test again with the failed utterance.

known_issues.symptom: Apex action returns 'System.LimitException: Apex CPU time limit exceeded'
known_issues.resolution: Optimise the loops in the action or move the work to an asynchronous Flow.

runbooks.title: Bulk Data Migration with Data Loader
runbooks.purpose: Loads cleansed legacy data into a Salesforce org in dependency order using Data Loader and the Bulk API. It protects data quality with load validation, reconciliation counts and a documented undo route.
prerequisites: The migration mapping workbook is approved by the client data owner
Source extracts are cleansed and deduplicated and stored on the firm's encrypted project drive
External ID fields exist on every object that receives loaded data
Validation rules, duplicate rules and triggers that could block the load are reviewed
Storage in the target org is at least 20 percent above the expected data size

steps.action: Take a full backup export of the target objects before any load.
steps.verification: The backup files are stored on the project drive and row counts are noted.

steps.action: Temporarily bypass non-essential automation using the agreed custom permission or custom setting.
steps.verification: A test insert of one row creates no automation side effects.

steps.action: Load a pilot of 500 Account rows with upsert on the external ID.
steps.verification: The success file has 500 rows and the error file is empty.

steps.action: Spot-check 25 pilot Accounts against the source for field accuracy.
steps.verification: All 25 match the source values.

steps.action: Load the full Account set with Bulk API 2.0 and a batch size of 2,000.
steps.verification: The success file row count equals the source row count.

steps.action: Load Contacts using the Account external ID as the parent reference.
steps.verification: The error file is empty or holds only rows already listed as expected rejects.

steps.action: Load Opportunities, Cases and other child objects in the order in the mapping workbook.
steps.verification: Each child object count matches the reconciliation sheet.

steps.action: Re-enable the bypassed automation.
steps.verification: The custom setting or permission shows the bypass switched off.

steps.action: Run the reconciliation report comparing source counts to loaded counts.
steps.verification: Every object shows a variance of 0 or an approved variance.

steps.action: Hold an 8 hour post-load monitoring window and check for automation failures and user-reported data issues.
steps.verification: No Flow or trigger fault emails arrive for the loaded objects.

rollback_steps: Stop all running Data Loader jobs.
Delete the loaded rows by their migration batch ID using a Data Loader delete job.
Confirm in the org that counts are back to the backup export figures.
Fix the source data or mapping and repeat the pilot load.
Notify the client data owner of the new migration date.

known_issues.symptom: Rows fail with 'UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW: unable to obtain exclusive access'
known_issues.resolution: Sort the file by parent ID, reduce the batch size to 200 and use serial mode, then rerun the failed rows.

known_issues.symptom: Rows fail with 'DUPLICATES_DETECTED'
known_issues.resolution: Review the duplicate rule matches, fix the source rows or enable the bypass setting for the migration user and reload.

known_issues.symptom: Job fails with 'STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: storage limit exceeded'
known_issues.resolution: Delete test data or ask the client to purchase additional data storage before restarting the load.

known_issues.symptom: Error 'REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: ConcurrentPerOrgLongTxn Limit exceeded'
known_issues.resolution: Pause other long-running jobs and rerun the load with a smaller batch size.

runbooks.title: MuleSoft API Deployment to Production
runbooks.purpose: Promotes a tested MuleSoft API application from the staging environment to production in Anypoint Platform and connects it to the live back-office systems. It also applies the security policies needed to expose the API safely to Salesforce.
prerequisites: MuleSoft Anypoint licences cover a production vCore for the application
The API specification is published in Anypoint Exchange and approved by the client technical contact
Staging end-to-end tests have passed with 0 critical defects
Production credentials for each connected system are stored in the secure properties vault
A technical contact is available at each connected system during the deployment window
Monitoring alerts are configured in Anypoint Monitoring

steps.action: Tag the application code in the repository with the release number.
steps.verification: The tag is visible in the remote repository and the build pipeline starts.

steps.action: Run the build pipeline to produce the deployable JAR with MUnit tests.
steps.verification: The pipeline shows all MUnit tests passing and test coverage of at least 80 percent.

steps.action: Update the production properties file with production endpoints and secure property keys.
steps.verification: A configuration diff against staging shows only environment values that differ.

steps.action: Deploy the application to the production environment in Runtime Manager.
steps.verification: The application status shows Running with a green health indicator.

steps.action: Run a health check call against the API's status endpoint.
steps.verification: The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the expected version number.

steps.action: Apply the client ID enforcement and rate limiting policies in API Manager.
steps.verification: A call without credentials returns HTTP 401.

steps.action: Test the throttling policy by sending 120 calls in one minute.
steps.verification: Calls above the limit return HTTP 429.

steps.action: Update the Salesforce named credential to use the production API URL.
steps.verification: A test callout from Salesforce returns HTTP 200.

steps.action: Run one end-to-end business scenario with real test data across Salesforce and the back-office system.
steps.verification: The data appears correctly in both systems.

steps.action: Enable the production alerts for error rate, response time and CPU.

steps.action: Begin the 48 hour monitoring window and check Anypoint Monitoring dashboards every 4 hours on the first day.

steps.action: Close the 48 hour window and record error rate and average response time in the release file.

rollback_steps: Switch the Salesforce named credential back to the previous endpoint or to a maintenance responder.
Stop the new application version in Runtime Manager.
Redeploy the previous application version from Anypoint Exchange.
Remove the new policy version in API Manager and reapply the previous one.
Run the health check and one end-to-end scenario on the restored version.
Notify the client technical contact and the connected system owners.

known_issues.symptom: Deployment stays in 'Deploying' and then fails with 'Application deployment timed out'
known_issues.resolution: Check that the vCore allocation is available and that the secure properties key matches, then redeploy.

known_issues.symptom: Calls return 'HTTP 503 Service Unavailable' from the API gateway
known_issues.resolution: Confirm the application is Running and has healthy workers; restart the application if a worker is stuck.

known_issues.symptom: Log shows 'javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed'
known_issues.resolution: Import the connected system's certificate chain into the application truststore and redeploy.

runbooks.title: Production Deployment Rollback
runbooks.purpose: Restores production to the last known good state when a release causes a business-critical defect. It sets out the decision, the technical reversal and the communication so the client is back in service quickly.
prerequisites: The last known good release tag or change set is identified
The delivery manager has approved a rollback after a Priority 1 or Priority 2 incident
A backup export of any data changed by the release exists
System Administrator access to production and to the source repository

steps.action: Open an incident and record the failing behaviour, the release number and the time first noticed.
steps.verification: The incident ticket holds all three details.

steps.action: Get written rollback approval from the delivery manager and the client business owner.
steps.verification: Both approvals are attached to the ticket.

steps.action: Freeze all other deployments and user changes to production metadata.
steps.verification: The freeze message is posted and acknowledged in the project channel.

steps.action: Deactivate new Flows, triggers and validation rules that cause the defect.
steps.verification: The Setup pages show the items as Inactive and the defect no longer reproduces.

steps.action: Validate the previous release against production with RunLocalTests.
steps.verification: The validation result shows Succeeded.

steps.action: Deploy the previous release and delete the components that exist only in the failed release using a destructive changes manifest.
steps.verification: The Deployment Status shows Succeeded with 0 failures.

steps.action: Repair data changed by the failed release from the backup export where the client approves it.
steps.verification: Spot-checked rows match the backup values.

steps.action: Run the smoke tests and keep a 2 hour monitoring window with the incident channel open.
steps.verification: All smoke tests pass and no new incidents are raised in the 2 hour window.

rollback_steps: If the rollback deployment fails, deploy the metadata in smaller groups starting with fields and objects.
If data repair fails, stop and restore the affected object from the backup export in a controlled load.
Escalate to the chief technology officer if the previous release cannot be validated.
Keep the freeze in place until the cause of the failed release is documented.

known_issues.symptom: Destructive deployment fails with 'Cannot delete custom field: field is referenced in a Flow'
known_issues.resolution: Deactivate and delete the Flow version that uses the field, then repeat the destructive deployment.

known_issues.symptom: Validation fails with 'Test failure: FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION'
known_issues.resolution: Temporarily deactivate the validation rule named in the error, deploy and reactivate it after the release.

known_issues.symptom: Component 'cannot be deleted because it has been modified since the deployment: Active Flow version'
known_issues.resolution: Make the previous Flow version active in the Flow Builder first and then delete the failed version.

runbooks.title: Experience Cloud Site Publish

Guest user and external user sharing rules are reviewed by the security lead
The accessibility check against WCAG 2.1 AA is passed
Test portal users exist for each user type
The custom domain and certificate are configured where a client domain is used

steps.action: Open Experience Builder in production and confirm the site template and theme are the release version.
steps.verification: The version label in Builder matches the release number.

steps.action: Review the guest user profile and sharing rules.
steps.verification: The guest user has no access to objects outside the approved list.

steps.action: Log in as each test portal user type and visit every page template.
steps.verification: Each user sees only the data allowed by the sharing model.

steps.action: Submit a test case through the self-service case form.
steps.verification: The case is created in the org with the correct owner and portal user.

steps.action: Test the knowledge search with 5 typical questions.
steps.verification: Each search returns the expected published article.

steps.action: Test the self-registration and password reset flows.
steps.verification: The test user receives the email and can log in.

steps.action: Click Publish in Experience Builder.
steps.verification: The confirmation email arrives and the site status shows Live.

steps.action: Load the public URL in a private browser window.
steps.verification: The page loads over HTTPS with the correct branding and no mixed content warnings.

steps.action: Hold a 12 hour monitoring window and check Login History and the site's error pages.

known_issues.symptom: Users see 'Insufficient Privileges: You don't have the level of access necessary'

known_issues.symptom: Publish fails with 'The site could not be published because of a validation error on a page'

runbooks.title: Marketing Cloud Journey Activation
runbooks.purpose: Activates a Journey Builder journey with its audience, emails and tracking in a Marketing Cloud account. It checks consent, sender authentication and test sends so that live sends do not damage deliverability.

The subscriber list has documented consent and the unsubscribe handling is configured

steps.action: Run Preview and Test Send on every email using 3 test subscribers.

steps.action: Run the spam and rendering checks on each email.

steps.action: Run journey validation in Journey Builder.

runbooks.title: Data Cloud Data Stream and Segment Activation

Each source system has a named data owner and a connection that can be used in production
The data model mapping document and identity resolution ruleset are approved

Data Cloud users hold the right Data Cloud permission sets

steps.action: Package the data streams, mappings and calculated insights and deploy them to production.

steps.action: Create the source connections in production using the production credentials.
steps.verification: Each connection test shows Connected.

steps.action: Start ingestion of each data stream with the scheduled frequency.

steps.action: Compare the ingested row counts with the source system counts.

steps.action: Check the field mappings in the data model for each stream.

steps.action: Review a sample of 30 unified profiles for merge accuracy.
steps.verification: At least 28 of the 30 profiles are merged correctly.

steps.action: Refresh the calculated insights and check the values for 5 known customers.
steps.verification: The values match the expected figures in the test sheet.

steps.action: Publish the segments and review the populations.
steps.verification: Each segment population is within 5 percent of the expected count.

steps.action: Activate the segments to the agreed destination.
steps.verification: The activation status shows Success and the destination receives the audience.

steps.action: Begin the 24 hour monitoring window and review stream refresh results and activation status at 8 hour intervals.
steps.verification: Every scheduled refresh in the window shows Successful.

rollback_steps: Pause the activation to the destination.
Stop the scheduled refresh of the new data streams.
Delete the segments and activations created by the release.
Delete the data streams that were created and any unified profiles built from them.
Repeat the validation in a sandbox before trying again.

known_issues.symptom: Data stream refresh fails with 'Error: Invalid credentials for the connector'
known_issues.resolution: Update the connection credentials with the data owner and run the refresh again.

known_issues.symptom: Identity resolution job shows 'Failed: matching rule has no valid fields'
known_issues.resolution: Map the matching fields to the unified Individual model and run the job again.

known_issues.symptom: Activation fails with 'Destination authentication expired'
known_issues.resolution: Reauthorise the destination connection and trigger the activation again.

runbooks.title: Revenue Cloud Pricing Rule Release
runbooks.purpose: Releases new or changed price books, pricing rules and discount schedules to production without disturbing open quotes. It uses test quotes with known expected prices to confirm that the pricing logic is correct.
prerequisites: The finance stakeholder has signed off the new price lists and discount policy
A pricing test sheet lists at least 25 scenarios with the expected net price
The pricing rules are deployed to a sandbox and all scenarios pass
A list of open quotes affected by the change has been produced

steps.action: Export the current price books, pricing rules and discount schedules from production.
steps.verification: The export files are stored on the project drive with counts noted.

steps.action: Deploy the pricing rule metadata to production using the Salesforce CLI Metadata Deployment from Source Control runbook.
steps.verification: The deployment shows Succeeded.

steps.action: Load the new price book entries with an upsert on the external ID.
steps.verification: The success file count equals the number of entries in the new price list.

steps.action: Activate the new price book and set the effective date.
steps.verification: The price book shows Active with the right effective date.

steps.action: Create test quotes for each of the 25 scenarios in the pricing test sheet.
steps.verification: Each quote net price matches the expected value to the cent.

steps.action: Test each approval path with a quote that crosses the discount threshold.
steps.verification: The quote routes to the named approver.

steps.action: Generate the quote document in each of the 2 templates.
steps.verification: The documents show correct totals, tax lines and terms.

steps.action: Review the open quotes in the affected list.
steps.verification: Each open quote keeps its original price or is flagged for repricing as agreed.

steps.action: Delete the test quotes created for validation.
steps.verification: A query for quotes with the test prefix returns 0 rows.

steps.action: Begin the 36 hour monitoring window and review new quotes and approval requests each morning.
steps.verification: No quote shows a price different from the price list by more than the approved discount.

rollback_steps: Deactivate the new price book and reactivate the previous one.
Deactivate the new pricing rules.
Reload the exported price book entries and rules from the backup files.
Reprice any quotes created during the faulty period with the finance stakeholder.
Notify the sales operations users of the restored prices.

known_issues.symptom: Quote line shows 'Error: Price book entry not found for product and currency'
known_issues.resolution: Add the missing price book entry for the product in the quote currency and recalculate the quote.

known_issues.symptom: Approval submit fails with 'No approver found for the approval step'
known_issues.resolution: Assign an approver or a queue to the approval step and resubmit the quote.

known_issues.symptom: Calculation fails with 'Apex CPU time limit exceeded' on large bundles
known_issues.resolution: Reduce the number of nested price rules on the bundle or split the bundle and recalculate.

runbooks.title: Record-Triggered Flow Deployment and Activation
runbooks.purpose: Deploys a tested Flow to production and activates it in a controlled way. It checks that the Flow version is correct and faults are visible to administrators from the moment it goes live.
prerequisites: The Flow has passed bulk testing with 200 rows in a sandbox
A fault path with an email alert to the admin group is configured
The Flow is deployed as inactive so that activation is a separate deliberate action

steps.action: Deploy the Flow metadata to production as an inactive version.
steps.verification: The Deployment Status shows Succeeded and the Flow shows Inactive in Setup.

steps.action: Review the entry criteria and the fault path in Flow Builder.
steps.verification: The entry criteria match the design document and the fault path sends to the admin group.

steps.action: Run the Flow debug with one test row in production using rollback mode.
steps.verification: The debug output shows the expected path and no rows are saved.

steps.action: Activate the new Flow version.
steps.verification: The version shows Active and the previous version is Obsolete.

steps.action: Create or update one test row that meets the entry criteria.
steps.verification: The expected field updates and related rows appear on the test row.

steps.action: Delete the test row and confirm the fault email address receives nothing.
steps.verification: No fault email is received and the row is in the recycle bin.

rollback_steps: Open the Flow in Setup and activate the previous version.
Deactivate the new version if there is no previous version.
Correct data changed by the Flow using the backup report.

known_issues.symptom: Flow fails with 'FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION: Required field missing'
known_issues.resolution: Populate the required field in the Flow or add an entry condition so the Flow does not run on incomplete data.

known_issues.symptom: Error 'Too many SOQL queries: 101' during a bulk update
known_issues.resolution: Move Get Records elements outside loops and use collections, then redeploy.

known_issues.symptom: Activation blocked with 'This flow version cannot be activated: a required element is not connected'
known_issues.resolution: Connect the unlinked element in Flow Builder and save before activating.

runbooks.title: Shield Platform Encryption Rollout
runbooks.purpose: Enables Shield Platform Encryption on the approved list of fields in a production org and confirms that search, reports and integrations still work. It also sets key management and backup so that data remains available.
prerequisites: Shield licences are purchased and the Shield Platform Encryption permission is granted to the administrator
The list of up to 20 fields to encrypt is approved by the client security contact
A tenant secret backup and key rotation procedure is agreed with the client
The Encryption Policy impact check has been run in a sandbox
Integrations, reports and SOQL queries that use the fields have been listed
A change window outside business hours is booked

steps.action: Review the field list against the data classification sheet.
steps.verification: Every field in the list has an approved classification.

steps.action: Deploy the same encryption settings to a Full sandbox and run the Encryption Statistics page.
steps.verification: Statistics show no blocked fields.

steps.action: Run the report, list view and SOQL tests that use the sandbox encrypted fields.
steps.verification: Each test returns the expected results or a documented limitation.

steps.action: In production, open Platform Encryption and generate the tenant secret.
steps.verification: The tenant secret appears with an Active status.

steps.action: Download and store the tenant secret backup in the approved key vault.
steps.verification: A key vault entry exists and a second person confirms access.

steps.action: Assign the Manage Encryption Keys permission to the named key custodians.
steps.verification: Only the named users appear in the permission set assignment list.

steps.action: Select the first batch of 10 fields in Encryption Policy and choose the deterministic or probabilistic scheme as approved.
steps.verification: The policy page lists the 10 fields as selected.

steps.action: Save the policy and start the background encryption of existing data.
steps.verification: The Encryption Statistics page shows the job as In Progress.

steps.action: Wait for the encryption job to finish.
steps.verification: The statistics page shows 100 percent of existing data encrypted for the first batch.

steps.action: Repeat the selection for the remaining approved fields in a second batch.
steps.verification: The statistics page shows Complete for every approved field.

steps.action: Run the production smoke tests on reports, search and the integrations listed.
steps.verification: All smoke tests pass or show only documented limitations.

steps.action: Check the Setup Audit Trail and Event Monitoring for the encryption changes.
steps.verification: The log shows each change made by the named administrator.

steps.action: Start the 72 hour monitoring window and review integration error logs every 12 hours.
steps.verification: The review log has an entry for each 12 hour check.

steps.action: Close the window and report the status to the client security contact.
steps.verification: The security contact confirms receipt of the report.

rollback_steps: Stop any running encryption job by contacting Salesforce Support if it cannot be cancelled in Setup.
Remove the affected fields from the Encryption Policy and save, then start decryption of existing data.
Wait for the statistics page to show the fields as not encrypted.
Restore any integration settings that were changed for encrypted fields.
Keep the tenant secret backup until the client security contact confirms it can be retired.

known_issues.symptom: Field selection fails with 'This field cannot be encrypted because it is used in a unique or external ID setting'
known_issues.resolution: Remove the unique or external ID setting, or choose the deterministic scheme where the field type allows it.

known_issues.symptom: Reports return 'Error: Filtering on an encrypted field uses a probabilistic scheme'
known_issues.resolution: Switch the field to the deterministic scheme or remove the filter from the report.

known_issues.symptom: SOQL fails with 'INVALID_FIELD: field is not filterable' on an encrypted field
known_issues.resolution: Remove the field from the WHERE or ORDER BY clause and apply the filter in code.

known_issues.symptom: Encryption job shows 'Failed: Insufficient storage while re-encrypting data'
known_issues.resolution: Free data storage or buy more, then restart the encryption job.
